finding.evidence: form with fields card, exp, cvv posted to http://
finding.description: Card numbers travel in clear and are handled by the shop itself.

recommendation.goal: What is the recommended fix for this web security flaw: card-data-over-http (Card numbers travel in clear and are handled by the shop itself. Evidence: form with fields card, exp, cvv posted to http://). State the concrete fix and cite a primary source (OWASP, MDN, NIST, PCI DSS, IETF RFC, or the vendor's own advisory).
recommendation.answer: Recommended fix: stop posting card, exp, cvv to http://. Serve checkout only over HTTPS with strong cryptography/TLS and trusted certificates, enforce HSTS, never transmit PAN in clear, and descope the shop by using a PCI DSS-compliant processor via redirect/hosted page/iframe/tokenization so the shop itself does not handle card data (SAQ-A model).

sources.contribution: Protect PAN in Transit is PCI DSS Requirement 4

fix.summary: Descope shop to SAQ-A: remove card form, ignore PAN and never store/echo it.
fix.risk: Checkout UX changes to PSP model; legacy card/exp/cvv fields are ignored.
